title: Origami latency decomposer 1412 p50/p95/p99 split by model & route with streaming vs non-streaming
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a cross-cutting observability artifact (metrics + traces + logs + Grafana panels) that decomposes p50/p95/p99 latency across model variants and API routes, with an explicit dimension for streaming vs non-streaming handling. Dashboard should allow engineers to pivot between: model family, model version, route, servepath stage (frontend, router, runtime, kv-cache), request shape (tokens_in/tokens_out), and I/O mode. Deliverables: telemetry schema changes, tracing hook placement and sampling guidance, log enrichment fields, Prometheus/TSDB aggregations, and Grafana dashboard JSON.
background: We often chase tail latency without a compact way to split signals by I/O mode. Several incidents showed streaming fallbacks inflating p99 while median remained stable; because traces are sampled aggressively, we lack a deterministic metric-based view that surfaces the root cause. Current dashboards are model- or route-centric but dont expose a combined streaming dimension or servepath breakdown. This ticket unblocks SRE and product owners to quickly identify whether regressions are introduced by model kernels, batching behavior, streaming I/O, or router fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: New Prometheus metric labels: model_name, model_version, route, io_mode (streaming|blocking), serve_stage (frontend|router|runtime|kvcache)
Tracing hooks added at router entry and runtime token loop with consistent trace IDs propagated and a low-overhead sampled path for tail analysis
Logs include enriched fields: request_id, model_variant, route, io_mode, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_id

Grafana dashboard delivered with panels: time-series p50/p95/p99 by (model, route) with io_mode split; cohort comparison view for request-shape buckets; waterfall decomposition panel showing serve_stage contributions
Dashboard supports drilldown links to trace viewer and the incident playbook
Docs and runbook updated with query examples and recommended alert thresholds for p95/p99 regressions per route
implementation_steps: 1) Define metric label additions and update exporters to attach io_mode and serve_stage
2) Add tracing hook points: router.receive -> router.dispatch -> runtime.start_token_loop -> runtime.kv_cache_lookup -> runtime.emit_chunk
3) Ensure deterministic propagation of request_id / trace_id across async streaming flows
4) Enrich structured logs emitted from runtime and router with new labels
4b) Add sampling policy for traces when p95/p99 above baseline to capture more tail traces
5) Create PromQL queries for p50/p95/p99 with label_join and histogram_quantile where needed
6) Build Grafana panels: model/route matrix, io_mode split lines, cohort pane, serve_stage waterfall
7) QA using synthetic workload generator (streaming and blocking mixes) and compare against golden traces
8) Ship dashboard JSON and update docs + alerting rules
notes: Avoid high-cardinality labels on metrics: keep model_version but cap route dimension cardinality via route hash mapping
For streaming requests, measure both first-chunk and completion latencies to separate head vs tail behavior
Consider derived metric for 'streaming_fallback_rate' when runtime falls back to blocking mode
Coordinate with infra team to ensure Prometheus scrape throughput can handle extra labels
This ticket complements ENG-741111 (latency-panorama) but focuses on explicit streaming decomposition and servepath waterfall
